content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "Initial Spares/Repair Parts (budget line 000999) is a U.S. Air Force procurement line funded in the Aircraft Procurement, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "59150fb60273b8db"}}, {"text": "Aircraft Initial Spares are required to fill the initial pipeline or inventory for all new aircraft systems, including modifications, support equipment, and other production categories, covering peculiar repairable and consumable components that must be available for issue at all levels of supply when newly fielded aircraft arrive.", "citation": {"fact_id": "aec2f5dcfc901035"}}, {"text": "Funding runs through two segments: Working Capital Fund spares, where the central procurement account reimburses the Working Capital Fund on delivery, and Exempt Spares, financed as a direct cite on the contract and covering items such as whole spare engines, contractor logistics support, and simulators and trainers.", "citation": {"fact_id": "aec2f5dcfc901035"}}, {"text": "Major Defense Acquisition Programs with funding in this line include the F-35, B-2, CV-22, KC-46A, MQ-9 Reaper, T-7A, F-15 EPAWSS, HH-60W, and MH-139A, among others.", "citation": {"fact_id": "aec2f5dcfc901035"}}, {"text": "FY 2026 spares support specific modernization efforts across the fleet, including B-2 communications suites, B-52 radar and data-link modernization, C-5 viability, C-17 modification kits, C-130H avionics modernization, and E-4B airborne-command-center upgrades.", "citation": {"fact_id": "91b7ef0c97e1121d"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding is $1,997,341 thousand (about $2.0 billion) requested for FY 2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "35d612e0b351a714"}}, {"text": "In FY 2024 the program recorded actual spending of $865,790 thousand (about $866 million), so the FY 2026 request is more than double its recent execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "9622b8bddb9c3a17"}}, {"text": "The FY 2026 request splits into a discretionary request of $973,535 thousand (about $974 million) and a reconciliation (mandatory) request of $1,023,806 thousand (about $1.02 billion).", "citation": {"fact_id": "d53ebd0829000145"}}, {"text": "The $1,023,806 thousand reconciliation (mandatory) portion is the larger half of the request and, combined with the discretionary base, produces the FY 2026 total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ad339eb8d41c65d2"}}, {"text": "Per the program narrative, the mandatory funding supports initial spares for air-vehicle propulsion, survivability, airframe, and avionics programs, with further detail in Section 20007 (Air Superiority) and Section 20010 (Readiness) of the Reconciliation Exhibit.", "citation": {"fact_id": "aec2f5dcfc901035"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Aircraft Procurement, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "db1e5469ca876aa7"}}, {"text": "Because this is a pooled spares line rather than a single platform, it channels money to the parent Major Defense Acquisition Programs it supports — among them the F-35, B-2, KC-46A, MQ-9 Reaper, and T-7A — with two new-start efforts in FY 2026 for B-2 Squadrons and the MQ-9 UAV.", "citation": {"fact_id": "91b7ef0c97e1121d"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
